title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 660-663 of the 140-3 manuscript). We are in the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', the elliptic or modular case.

- 𝔖^+ is a profinite completion of the modular group. Examples are \hat{SL_2(Z)}, or the congruence completion SL(2,Ẑ) as the explicitly named non-degenerate case. 𝔖^𝔖 is a distinguished subgroup.
- ρ and σ are the elliptic generators of orders 3 and 2.
- L_0 is the cusp (parabolic) subgroup generated by ξ_0, the image of Ẑ → 𝔖^+, n ↦ ξ_0^n.
- Z_{ρ,σ} consists of quadruples (u, μ, ε, ε') with u ∈ Aut, μ ∈ Ẑ^* (the cyclotomic exponent on the cusp) and ε, ε' ∈ μ (signs or exponents on ρ, σ).
- G_{ρ,σ}^𝔖 is a group of 'Teichmüller-type' symmetries, built as a subquotient of S_0G = Z_{ρ,σ}·𝔖^+.

The previous page gives an exact sequence 1 → L_0 → Z_0 → G → \tilde G → 1. Its last map records the full datum (u, μ, ε, ε').

On this page Grothendieck forgets μ and looks at the coarser map (45):
- The map is G_{ρ,σ}^𝔖 → Aut(𝔖^+)×μ×μ, u ↦ (int(u)|𝔖^+, ε_3(u), ε_2(u)).
- By (38), its image (46) consists of the (u, ε_3, ε_2) such that:
  - (a) u(ρ) is 𝔖^𝔖-conjugate to ρ^{ε_3};
  - (b) u(σ) is 𝔖^𝔖-conjugate to σ^{ε_2};
  - (c) u(L_0) is 𝔖^𝔖-conjugate to L_0;
  - (d) u stabilises 𝔖^𝔖, which is automatic when ε_3 = ε_2 by (a) and (b).
- The kernel (47) consists of the classes f^{-1}·(int f, μ, 1, 1) with f ∈ 𝔖^𝔖. These are the inner automorphisms that also normalise the cusp, together with a compatible cyclotomic exponent μ.

To analyse this kernel he sets SN_0 = Norm_{𝔖^+}(L_0) and SN_0^𝔖 = SN_0 ∩ 𝔖^𝔖. He also defines \tilde{SN}_0 = {(u, μ) ∈ SN_0 × Ẑ^* : u ξ_0 u^{-1} = ξ_0^μ}.
- The projection \tilde{SN}_0^𝔖 → SN_0^𝔖 is an isomorphism (50) when Ẑ → L_0 is injective, since μ is then determined by u.
- He gives the canonical injective homomorphism (51): \tilde{SN}_0^𝔖 → S_0G = Z_{ρ,σ}·𝔖^+, (f, μ) ↦ f^{-1}·(int f, μ, 1, 1). It extends (42) and restricts on L_0 to the canonical map (28).

The next page concludes with an exact sequence 1 → L_0 → \tilde{SN}_0 → G → \tilde{\tilde G} → 1. Hence Ker(45) ≅ \tilde{SN}_0^𝔖 / L_0^𝔖.

Purpose: to measure how much finer G_{ρ,σ} is than the naive 'group of automorphisms of 𝔖^+ preserving the elliptic and parabolic inertia conjugacy classes'. The discrepancy is exactly the normaliser of the cusp modulo the cusp.
- In the congruence case SL(2,Ẑ), SN_0 is the Borel subgroup of matrices (a b; 0 a^{-1}). The quotient SN_0/L_0 is then ≅ Ẑ^*, the diagonal torus, acting on ξ_0 by μ = a^2. So the kernel is large: (45) fails to be injective 'even in non-degenerate cases such as SL(2,Ẑ)'.
- For the full profinite completion of SL_2(Z) one expects the normaliser of the cusp to be much smaller, roughly ±1 × L_0.
errors: The notation drifts between N_0^𝔖 and SN_0^𝔖 in (49), and between \tilde{SN}_0 and \tilde N_0 (written above, later corrected by the marginal 'idem pour \tilde{SN}_0').
In (49) the condition 'u(ξ_0)=ξ_0^μ' should be read as conjugation, int(u)(ξ_0) = ξ_0^μ. The page uses u both for an element of SN_0 and for an automorphism.
In (48) the quantifier 'μ ∈ Ẑ^*_?' is unclear in the handwriting.

The parenthetical claim about (45) reads in the transcription as 'effectivement injectif'. The kernel computed on this page and the next (≅ \tilde{SN}_0/L_0, which is ≅ Ẑ^* for SL(2,Ẑ)) shows the intended meaning is that (45) is NOT injective, even in the non-degenerate case 𝔖^+ = SL(2,Ẑ).

ideas.what: Group G_{ρ,σ} of symmetries of a profinite modular group preserving the conjugacy classes of the elliptic generators (up to signs) and of the cusp subgroup (with a cyclotomic exponent μ), mapped to Aut(𝔖^+)×μ×μ, with the image characterised by inertia-preservation conditions
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group for M_{1,1}; inertia-preserving ('braid-like') automorphisms of \hat{SL_2(Z)}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto, Lochak–Schneps; Grothendieck's Esquisse for the programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the Teichmüller tower and GT idea; the detailed elliptic construction appears in the unpublished Longue Marche sequel material

ideas.what: Kernel of the 'forgetful' map identified with the normaliser of the cusp modulo the cusp, \tilde{SN}_0/L_0, via an explicit exact sequence
ideas.modern_name: Normaliser of a parabolic (inertia) subgroup modulo the subgroup; Borel modulo unipotent radical in the congruence case

ideas.what: Extended normaliser \tilde{SN}_0 of pairs (f, μ) with f ξ_0 f^{-1} = ξ_0^μ, embedded into the semidirect product Z_{ρ,σ}·𝔖^+
ideas.modern_name: Cyclotomic twisting of inertia; normaliser with character

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly observes that for the congruence completion SL(2,Ẑ) the inertia-preserving symmetry group carries a large extra kernel: the cusp normaliser (Borel) modulo the cusp, ≅ Ẑ^*. So his finer group G_{ρ,σ} is not detected by Aut(𝔖^+) together with the signs. This is a small, precise structural remark on GT-like groups for congruence versus full profinite completions. It is consistent with known facts and probably not new to specialists.
missed.quote: même dans des cas pas du tout dégénérés tels que 𝔖^+ = Sl(2,Ẑ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It touches the comparison of GT-type actions on \hat{SL_2(Z)} versus its congruence quotient (congruence subgroup problem, Boggi/Hain–Matsumoto style questions). However, it is a routine computation.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine bookkeeping step: exact sequences describing the kernel and image of a forgetful map for a Teichmüller-type group in the elliptic case. It is historically interesting as unpublished detail of Grothendieck's 'modular' anabelian programme, but contains no result a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: The parenthesis after (45) most likely says the map is NOT injective ('non injectif'), consistent with the kernel computed in (47)-(52bis).
In (47) the elements are written f^{-1}·u, i.e. f^{-1}·(u, μ, 1, 1) with u = int(f). The transcription reads 'f^{\underline u}'.
In (49) the overwritten symbol is \tilde N_0 / \tilde{SN}_0; the marginal note reads 'idem pour \tilde{SN}_0'.
The page number at the top is 634 (overwritten from 633).
